Jump to: Contact us Reimagining higher education partnerships SOAS's Strategic Plan articulates a vision for a new model of international partnerships that is responsive to the transnational character of our global challenges. There is an urgent need for international partnerships which are more equitable in nature, requiring a fundamental rethinking of partnership models to enable the co-development, co-teaching and co-accreditation of academic programmes in a much more integrated way. Our vision Play video Visit SOAS If you and your delegation would like to visit us in London to discuss plans to collaborate or if you have any questions about our partnerships, please get in touch. Send us a message Partnership models Joint programmes Open Universities often talk about equitable partnerships but there is little understanding of what this truly means. This is because it is difficult to establish equitable partnerships in an unequal world. Instead, most partnerships concern student mobility, often taking the form of international exchanges or dual degrees – students begin their studies at one institution and move to another. But what is needed are joint programmes that bring knowledge systems into conversation with each other so that we can tackle the transnational challenges facing us today. With our new equitable partnerships, we aim to do just this. These unique programmes developed in partnership with institutions across Africa, Asia and the Middle East are co-designed, co-taught and co-accredited with a single fee charged to all students. Each programme explores a key global issue from a Global South-Global North perspective, providing students with a rich learning experience that crosses knowledge systems. Dual programmes Open SOAS is working with a growing number of university partners to offer students a range of dual degree programmes (at undergraduate and postgraduate level), as well as progression and articulation arrangements. Dual degrees provide students with the opportunity to take degrees at (and receive two separate awards from) two different universities in a shorter amount of time than it would take to complete both degrees separately. to: Contact us Guidance for international applicants Agent representatives support international students with their applicant journey on behalf of SOAS. This includes providing guidance on best-fit degree programmes, support with completing applications, and offering post-application guidance across topics such as student visas, accommodation, and funding. Each approved agent listed below is carefully selected by the SOAS International Office and holds a direct contract with the university. This ensures that they are equipped with regular training, resources, and comprehensive knowledge to accurately advise applicants and represent SOAS. Where an applicant enrols through an approved agent, a monetary commission fee will be paid directly to the representative in recognition of services provided. All applications to SOAS are assessed equally according to our standard entry requirements and criteria. It is not compulsory to apply through an approved agent representative. If you are considering working with an agent, we recommend you read the British Council's guide to choosing an education agent . UK Agent Quality Framework Open SOAS University of London is committed to the UK Agent Quality Framework and pledges to create and maintain the highest standards of agent management, ensuring the UK remains a leading study destination for international students. The UK Agent Quality Framework (AQF) is an initiative led by the UK government and sector partners to promote professional and ethical standards among educational advisors representing UK institutions. It sets out a shared set of expectations and best practice to ensure that prospective students receive accurate, reliable, and trustworthy advice throughout their education journey. Our collaboration with global representatives is guided by the Agent Quality Framework (AQF), and we regularly review and monitor their work to ensure continued alignment with these standards. This enables SOAS to provide international students with a high-quality experience from the moment they begin exploring their options to their arrival at SOAS and beyond. Complaints process Open We are committed to working with education agents and advisors who provide honest, transparent, and student-focused support. If you have concerns about the behaviour or practices of an agent representing SOAS, we encourage you to let us know. We take all complaints seriously and will investigate any concerns raised about misrepresentation, unethical conduct, or a failure to meet expected standards. How to submit a complaint If you have a concern about an education agent representing SOAS, please complete the online complaints form with as much detail as possible. SOAS will acknowledge receipt of the complaint within five working days. All complaints will be handled confidentially and in accordance with our Educational Advisor and Agent Complaints Policy . Guide to choosing and education agent Open If you are considering working with an agent, we recommend you read the British Council's student and parent guide to choosing an education agent . This guide, part of the UK Agent Quality Framework (AQF), helps you understand what to look for in an agent, key questions to ask, and how to avoid poor practices. It also links to the National Code of Ethical Practice for UK Education Agents and the British Council’s UK Certified Counsellor Database . to: Contact us Guidance for international applicants Agent representatives support international students with their applicant journey on behalf of SOAS. This includes providing guidance on best-fit degree programmes, support with completing applications, and offering post-application guidance across topics such as student visas, accommodation, and funding. Each approved agent listed below is carefully selected by the SOAS International Office and holds a direct contract with the university. This ensures that they are equipped with regular training, resources, and comprehensive knowledge to accurately advise applicants and represent SOAS. Where an applicant enrols through an approved agent, a monetary commission fee will be paid directly to the representative in recognition of services provided. All applications to SOAS are assessed equally according to our standard entry requirements and criteria. It is not compulsory to apply through an approved agent representative. If you are considering working with an agent, we recommend you read the British Council's guide to choosing an education agent . UK Agent Quality Framework Open SOAS University of London is committed to the UK Agent Quality Framework and pledges to create and maintain the highest standards of agent management, ensuring the UK remains a leading study destination for international students. The UK Agent Quality Framework (AQF) is an initiative led by the UK government and sector partners to promote professional and ethical standards among educational advisors representing UK institutions. It sets out a shared set of expectations and best practice to ensure that prospective students receive accurate, reliable, and trustworthy advice throughout their education journey. Our collaboration with global representatives is guided by the Agent Quality Framework (AQF), and we regularly review and monitor their work to ensure continued alignment with these standards. This enables SOAS to provide international students with a high-quality experience from the moment they begin exploring their options to their arrival at SOAS and beyond. Complaints process Open We are committed to working with education agents and advisors who provide honest, transparent, and student-focused support. If you have concerns about the behaviour or practices of an agent representing SOAS, we encourage you to let us know. We take all complaints seriously and will investigate any concerns raised about misrepresentation, unethical conduct, or a failure to meet expected standards. How to submit a complaint If you have a concern about an education agent representing SOAS, please complete the online complaints form with as much detail as possible. SOAS will acknowledge receipt of the complaint within five working days. All complaints will be handled confidentially and in accordance with our Educational Advisor and Agent Complaints Policy . Guide to choosing and education agent Open If you are considering working with an agent, we recommend you read the British Council's student and parent guide to choosing an education agent . This guide, part of the UK Agent Quality Framework (AQF), helps you understand what to look for in an agent, key questions to ask, and how to avoid poor practices. It also links to the National Code of Ethical Practice for UK Education Agents and the British Council’s UK Certified Counsellor Database . here: Home International Global Partnerships SOAS–Sophia University Graduate Dual Degree Programme The Department of Japan and Korea at SOAS, in collaboration with Sophia University's Graduate Programme in Global Studies (GPGS) is delighted to offer a Graduate Dual Degree Programme. The Dual MA is based at Sophia University, as Japanese Master’s programmes are typically 2-years long, and SOAS contributes to it by offering its MA in Japanese Studies as an option for students originally enrolled at Sophia University. For SOAS students there is the opportunity to continue studying in Japan for a further year after first completing the MA in Japanese Studies at SOAS. Students proceeding to Sophia University can add any one degree within the GPGS at Sophia University, while students coming from Sophia must choose the MA Japanese Studies from SOAS. Students will study 1-year at GPGS and 1-year at SOAS. Only upon successful completion of both the MA Japanese Studies at SOAS and the corresponding 1-year element at Sophia will students receive two MA degrees, one from each institution. For students considering enrolment through SOAS Applications are made to the 1-year MA Japanese Studies programme at SOAS. The continuation at Sophia is an optional add-on that has no impact on how the MA Japanese Studies is taught at SOAS and its normal rules and regulations apply. For students considering enrolment through SOAS, this is an opportunity to add one year of study at Sophia University, after they have completed the taught elements of their MA in Japanese Studies with SOAS. However, students should indicate interest in the possibility to continue to Sophia University upon the point of application. Only upon being accepted by Sophia University in a separate application procedure (please see below), can the students proceed to Japan. The fees for the MAs are to be paid separately to each institution.
